root.name: Dutch Defense: Semi-Leningrad Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. g3 Nf6 3. Bg2 g6

overview: Against the fianchetto set-up Black plays the Leningrad formation (...g6, ...Bg7, ...d6, ...O-O) with a fianchetto of his own. After 4.Nf3 Bg7 5.O-O O-O 6.c4 d6 Black prepares ...Qe8, ...Nc6 and ...e5. White aims for the d5 or d4-d5 advance and the c4/Nc3 build-up against the f5 pawn and e4; Black aims for a kingside attack with ...e5 and ...Ng4.

white_ideas.idea: Build c4, Nc3, d5 and use the long diagonal to restrain the Dutch centre.
Prepare e4 or Qc2 and Rb1 with b4 to attack on the queenside.

black_ideas.idea: Play ...d6, ...Qe8, ...Nc6 and ...e5 to strike at the centre and attack on the kingside.
Fianchetto Bg7 and aim ...Ne4 and ...Ng4 for an attack with pieces and pawn pushes.

typical_structures.structure: Leningrad pawn centre with Black pawns on f5, d6 and e5 against White's c4/d4 centre, kings castled short.

character.notes: The Dutch is unbalanced by design: Black weakens e8-h5 and plays for kingside attack while White presses in the centre and on the queenside.

soundness.notes: Fully playable; used by strong players.

structure.notes: Centre in tension with ...e5 and d5 possible, leaving the structure undecided.

approach.notes: A main branch of the Dutch, played by strong players.

level.notes: The Leningrad plans (...e5, kingside attack, timing of ...Qe8) are subtle and need understanding more than memory.
